newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on late foreign buying of blue chips, brokers said.
The all share index rose 3.32 points to 577.70.
"We could fill the Sampath order only by moving up on the price," said Manjula Kumarasinghe of brokerage Jardine Fleming, referring to blue chip Sampath Bank wrich rose 3.25 rupees to 47 rupees.
Sampath Bank accounted for about one sixth of the total volume. Of the total turnover of 17.84 million rupees, foreign buying totalled 13.4 million rupees and selling 1.5 million.
Price gains led falls by 26 to 12.
Brokers said retail investors were active among liquid, low-priced shares in the plantation, finance and manufacturing sectors, brokers said.
"Some booked profits today while others returned with profits they made yesterday," said a trader at brokerage John Keells.
Among blue chips, Ceylon Tobacco rose one rupee to 28.50 and John Keells Holdings two to 175.
